articles.title: Psychological resilience may buffer children’s brains against some effects of abuse
articles.summary: New brain imaging research suggests resilience matters for children who have been abused. Among less resilient kids, abuse was tied to stronger links between emotional and bodily brain networks, which in turn tracked with more physical symptoms and depression.

articles.title: Faces and bodies send matching signals of attractiveness, but voices tell a different story
articles.summary: A recent study shows that a person's facial and bodily attractiveness are closely linked in the eyes of observers. However, the human voice operates independently, sending a separate biological message to potential partners.

articles.title: As America shifted left under Trump, emotional hostility widened the partisan gap
articles.summary: During Donald Trump’s first presidency, American public opinion broadly shifted leftward. But a new study reveals this "liberal rebound" was accompanied by surging emotional hostility between political parties, driving voters further apart on key policy issues.

articles.title: Brain structure linked to how well patients respond to an antidepressant, small study finds
articles.summary: Why do some people with depression respond to medication while others don't? A small study points to the brain's outer layer, finding that the folding complexity and thickness of certain cortical regions tracked how much patients improved.

articles.title: Glucosamine, a popular joint supplement, linked to faster Alzheimer’s progression
articles.summary: A large health-record analysis found that glucosamine use was associated with a 25% higher likelihood of mild cognitive impairment progressing to dementia. Lab experiments suggest the popular joint supplement may intensify an abnormal sugar-tagging process in the Alzheimer’s brain, although researchers say clinical trials are needed to determine whether it actually causes harm.

articles.title: Why rheumatoid arthritis pain may persist even when inflammation is under control
articles.summary: Pain and fatigue in rheumatoid arthritis can persist even after inflammation improves, with depression, poor sleep, obesity, smoking, and chronic pain potentially helping sustain symptoms. Researchers say identifying these hidden drivers could prevent unnecessary medication changes and lead to more personalized treatment.

articles.title: REM sleep paradox: Dreaming may drain the brain’s energy even as fuel supply rises
articles.summary: Scientists discovered a surprising energy paradox in the brain during REM sleep, the stage most closely associated with dreaming. Blood supply to the brain begins increasing even before REM starts, but neurons’ immediately available energy, measured as ATP, then drops. The finding suggests that dreaming may require such intense internal processing that neurons consume energy faster than it can be replenished.

articles.title: SMARtCARE: Privacy-Preserving Agentic AI Systems for Bounded-Autonomy Clinical Decision Support
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.31763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-context clinical AI systems can miss relevant patient history when prior admissions fall outside the active reasoning context. In ICU monitoring, this can cause early vital-sign drift to appear nonspecific even when it resembles a prior deterioration pattern. SMARtCARE addresses this gap through a four-state clinical decision-support architecture: Stable, Meta-cognitive, Assisted, and Regulated (Revoked). Rather than automatically retrieving prior records, SMARtCARE uses a lossy six-channel fingerprint of the patient's prior trajectory. When
